title: Mapping fibers determined by a cartesian edge
statement:
Use quasicategories, right-pinched mapping spaces, homotopy fibers and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], postcomposition of mapping spaces by an edge as in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], and inner fibrations and horn-cartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $p:E\to B$ be an inner fibration of quasicategories in a fixed universe, let $e:y\to z$ be a $p$-cartesian edge, and put $s=p(y)$, $t=p(z)$ and $f=p(e)$. Write $E_s=E\times_B\{s\}$ for the degreewise fiber. For every $w\in E_s$, coherent postcomposition with $e$ induces an equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{E_s}(w,y)\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{f}\bigl(\operatorname{Map}_E(w,z)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_B(s,t)\bigr).$$
The mapping spaces in this formula are Kan complexes. The equivalence is natural under functors over $B$ which carry the specified cartesian edge to a cartesian edge: if $p':E'\to B$ is another inner fibration and $T:E\to E'$ satisfies $p'T=p$ and $T(e)$ is $p'$-cartesian, then the square between these equivalences for $(w,e)$ and $(T(w),T(e))$ commutes up to homotopy; its left map is the map induced by $T_s:E_s\to E'_s$ and its right map is the induced map of homotopy fibers. No existence of cartesian lifts other than the specified edge is required.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 5.1.3.11 (01U8), restricted to cartesian edges, with Proposition 4.6.1.22 for mapping Kan fibrations, Proposition 3.4.0.7 for homotopy fibers, and Proposition 4.6.5.10 for the natural right-pinched comparison. Naturality is that of postcomposition. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived. Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag.

proof.text: Fix $w\in E_s$ and abbreviate $A=\operatorname{Map}_{E_s}(w,y)$, $M=\operatorname{Map}_E(w,z)$, $N=\operatorname{Map}_B(s,t)$ and $M_f=M\times_N\{f\}$. The fiber $E_s$ is a quasicategory: a lifting problem for an inner horn in $E_s$ is the lifting problem for $p$ with lower simplex constant at $s$, and its filler remains over $s$, by [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Thus $A,M,N$ are Kan complexes by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. The map $q:M\to N$ is a Kan fibration by [lem-coef-infinity-inner-mapping-fiber]. Its strict fiber $M_f$ is Kan: a horn in it lifts through $q$ over the constant simplex at $f$. We will construct postcomposition in this strict fiber, rather than assert that an arbitrary representative of an absolute composition class is strictly over $f$.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.3.11 and Notation 5.1.3.10: relative mapping space over the fixed base edge; Kan input from Proposition 4.6.1.22 (01P8).

proof.text: Define a simplicial set $Q$ as follows. A degree-$n$ simplex is a map $\sigma:\Delta^{n+2}\to E$ whose entire face on $\{0,\ldots,n\}$ is constant at $w$, whose vertex $n+1$ is $y$, whose last edge $\{n+1,n+2\}$ is $e$, and whose composite with $p$ is $f\circ\rho_n$, where $\rho_n:[n+2]\to[1]$ sends $0,\ldots,n+1$ to $0$ and $n+2$ to $1$. For $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, use the extension $[m+2]\to[n+2]$ equal to $\alpha$ on the first $m+1$ vertices and sending the two final vertices to $n+1,n+2$. These operators preserve all conditions and obey the simplicial identities. Restricting to the faces omitting the last vertex and the penultimate vertex gives simplicial maps $a:Q\to A$ and $b:Q\to M_f$, respectively. The first face lies entirely over $s$; the second lies over the degenerate $n$-simplex of the mapping-space vertex $f$, exactly as required by the right-pinched definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Explicit right-pinched version of the relative triangle correspondence in Notation 5.1.3.10 (01U7); all operators and restrictions are given here.

proof.text: The map $a$ lifts every boundary inclusion $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, including $n=0$. Indeed a degree-$n$ lifting problem specifies the faces $d_0\sigma,\ldots,d_n\sigma$ by its boundary in $Q$ and the face $d_{n+2}\sigma$ by its given simplex of $A$. Together with the prescribed edge $e$ these are the horn $\Lambda_{n+1}^{n+2}$ in $E$, over $f\rho_n$ in $B$. Their intersections agree because the square is commutative and the boundary is simplicial. For $n=0$ this is the two-edge horn with edges $w\to y$ and $e:y\to z$; thus the empty boundary case is included. The inner-fibration clause of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] fills the horn, since $0<n+1<n+2$. The filler has the required constant initial face, final edge and base image, so is a lift in $Q$. By the boundary-lifting characterization in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], $a$ is a trivial Kan fibration and a weak homotopy equivalence. In particular $Q$ is Kan, since a horn in $Q$ can first be filled in $A$ and then lifted through the Kan fibration $a$.

source.place: Direct inner-horn argument for the relative composition correspondence underlying Notation 5.1.3.10; boundary degree n becomes the inner horn of dimension n+2 missing face n+1.

proof.text: The map $b$ also lifts every $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$. The boundary in $Q$ specifies $d_0\sigma,\ldots,d_n\sigma$, while the given simplex of $M_f$ specifies $d_{n+1}\sigma$. Along with $e$, their union is $\Lambda_{n+2}^{n+2}$, again over $f\rho_n$. For $n=0$ its edges are $w\to z$ and $e:y\to z$, so this case also has the required prescribed final edge. In every dimension the ordered last edge is precisely $\{n+1,n+2\}$ and its image is $e$. Hence the $p$-cartesian horn condition of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] provides a filler. Its initial face is constant at $w$, its penultimate vertex is $y$, its final edge is $e$, and its base is $f\rho_n$, so it is a lift in $Q$. Consequently $b$ is a trivial Kan fibration and a weak homotopy equivalence by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. This proves the equivalence of the span $A\xleftarrow{a}Q\xrightarrow{b}M_f$ directly; the cartesian mapping-fiber theorem itself has not been used as a premise.

source.place: Direct final-horn proof of the forward implication of Proposition 5.1.3.11, specialized to a cartesian edge; boundary degree n becomes the horn of dimension n+2 missing its final face.

proof.text: Choose a section $r:A\to Q$ of $a$ by lifting the monomorphism $\varnothing\hookrightarrow A$. This is possible because [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] expresses every monomorphism as a transfinite composite of pushouts of boundary inclusions, against all of which $a$ lifts by Step 3. Lifting along the endpoint inclusion $Q\times\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow Q\times\Delta^1$, with upper maps $\mathrm{id}_Q$ and $ra$ and lower map $a\,\mathrm{pr}_Q$, gives a simplicial homotopy $h:\mathrm{id}_Q\simeq ra$ satisfying $ah=a\,\mathrm{pr}_Q$: the lower maps agree on the two endpoints since $ar=\mathrm{id}_A$. Thus $r$ is a homotopy inverse to $a$. Define $c_e=br:A\to M_f$. Since $a$ and $b$ are weak homotopy equivalences, the two-out-of-three property of the model structure in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], applied to $ar=\mathrm{id}_A$, shows that $r$ and then $c_e$ are weak homotopy equivalences. These sections are choices from the explicit boundary-lifting construction, and their homotopy class is fixed by $[c_e]=[b][a]^{-1}$.

source.place: Choice-independent representative of the relative composition class: section and endpoint-cylinder lifts; compare Stacks 08NM (lemma-trivial-kan) and 08NS (lemma-trivial-kan-homotopy), whose lifting argument is written out here.

proof.text: We check that $c_e$ is the coherent postcomposition required in the statement. Write $j$ for the natural right-pinch map of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], and let $V(w,y,z)$, $\theta$ and $\ell$ be the triangle space and restrictions of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Precomposition with the monotone map $[2]\times[n]\to[n+2]$ sending $(0,i)$ to $i$, $(1,i)$ to $n+1$ and $(2,i)$ to $n+2$ sends $\sigma\in Q_n$ to a simplex of $V(w,y,z)$. This construction commutes with every simplicial operator. Its restrictions to $01$, $12$ and $02$ are respectively $j(a\sigma)$, the constant simplex at $e$, and $j(b\sigma)$, with $a\sigma$ viewed in $\operatorname{Map}_E(w,y)$. Hence $\theta v=(e,j a)$ and $\ell v=j b$ exactly. Since $[\theta]$ is invertible by the cited composition statement, its defining equation gives $[j][b]=[j]\,[e\circ-]\,[a]$. Cancel the homotopy equivalence $[j]$ and then $[a]$ to see that $[b][a]^{-1}$, followed by $M_f\hookrightarrow M$, is the specified absolute postcomposition class restricted to $A$. The construction through $Q$ retains its strict base $f$, and so provides the relative coherent postcomposition representative, not only its map on components.

source.place: Comparison of the explicit relative triangle span with the composition law of Notation 5.1.3.10 and the natural right-pinched comparison of Proposition 4.6.5.10 (01L5).

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] with $U=M$, $u=q:M\to N$, $V=\Delta^0$ and $v=f:\Delta^0\to N$. All three spaces are Kan by Step 1, and $u$ is a Kan fibration. The strict pullback is $M_f$; its path pullback is $M\times_{N,\mathrm{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,N)\times_{\mathrm{ev}_1,N}\{f\}$, exactly the homotopy fiber in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], with paths directed from $q(m)$ to $f$. The comparison $k:M_f\to\operatorname{hofib}_f(q)$ sends $m$ to $(m,\mathrm{const}_f)$ and is a weak homotopy equivalence. Thus $kc_e$ is the required equivalence. The homotopy fiber is Kan by the same comparison lemma's first assertion.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.7 (0329) and Construction 3.4.0.3 (010B), in the order M, point, so paths go from q(m) to f.

proof.text: For $T:E\to E'$ over $B$, composition of every defining simplex with $T$ gives $t_Q:Q\to Q'$ and the induced maps $t_A:A\to A'$ and $t_f:M_f\to M'_f$. Because $p'T=p$, all base simplices remain $f\rho_n$, and the face restrictions give exact equalities $a't_Q=t_Aa$ and $b't_Q=t_fb$. The assumption that $T(e)$ is cartesian makes Step 4 valid for $b'$. With sections $r,r'$ chosen in Step 5, compose the homotopy $h':\mathrm{id}_{Q'}\simeq r'a'$ with $t_Qr$; since $a't_Qr=t_A$, this gives $t_Qr\simeq r't_A$. Composing with $b'$ proves $t_fc_e=t_fbr=b't_Qr\simeq b'r't_A=c_{T(e)}t_A$. Finally the path-pullback map sends $(m,\gamma)$ to $(T(m),\gamma)$, and therefore carries $(m,\mathrm{const}_f)$ to $(T(m),\mathrm{const}_f)$ exactly. It commutes with $k$. Composing the preceding homotopy with this constant-path comparison gives precisely the asserted square of homotopy-fiber equivalences, with left map induced by $T_s$ and right map the induced homotopy-fiber map. Only $e$ and $T(e)$ entered any cartesian horn lifting.

source.place: Naturality of the constructed relative triangle span and constant-path comparison; the choice-of-section homotopy is given explicitly rather than asserted to restrict from an absolute homotopy.

proof_origin.place: Direct right-pinched relative triangle proof of the cartesian case of Proposition 5.1.3.11: boundary lifts are inner horns and final cartesian horns in dimension n+2. Identifies the span with coherent composition, then uses the existing Kan strict/path comparison and explicit section homotopies for naturality. No appeal to Proposition 5.1.3.11 as a dependency.
